travel.title: TRAVEL
travel.intro:
San Juan Island is - well yes, you guessed it - an island! That means it's surrounded by water, so you will either arrive by boat or plane, unless you are an excellent swimmer. 

From Seattle, here are your options:

steps.body:
First, get to the Anacortes ferry terminal. It's roughly 2 hours north of Seattle-Tacoma airport (SEA) and 1 hour 15 mins from Paine Field airport (PAE). You can rent a car or take an airport shuttle to get there from either airport.  

Then, take the ferry from Anacortes to Friday Harbor (about ~1 hour, scenic, and fun!)

**Walking on?** No reservation needed - just buy a ticket at the terminal. There's long-term parking at the ferry terminal and Friday Harbor is very walkable. 
**Bringing a car?** Reserve a spot both ways on [WSDOT](https://secureapps.wsdot.wa.gov/ferries/reservations/vehicle/SailingSchedule.aspx?cookieCheck=true) and drive your car right on the ferry. 

Washington State Ferries releases vehicle reservations in phases, and they tend to fill quickly. The first reservations for our wedding date will become available in mid-April 2027, so be sure to check back or [set a calendar reminder](ferry-reminder.ics).

steps.label: SEATTLE → FRIDAY HARBOR
steps.body:
If you'd like, skip the drive and ferry with a flight directly into Friday Harbor. Faster, more expensive, and objectively very cool. Some options:

**Seaplane** — Kenmore Air floatplanes leave from Lake Union and land in Friday Harbor's marina, a few blocks from downtown (~45 min flight time).  SeaTac to Lake Union is roughly a ~20 min drive. 

**Wheeled plane** — Kenmore Air Express flies from Boeing Field (~35 min; they run a shuttle from SeaTac) or from Paine Field (~25 min) into Friday Harbor Airport, less than a mile from town. If you're connecting through Paine Field, you can book the whole thing as one ticket through [Alaska Airlines] (https://alaskaair.com).
Friday Harbor is very walkable, and we’ll provide transportation to and from the welcome event on Friday and wedding on Saturday. If you want to explore beyond town, bring a car.

stays.name: FRIDAY HARBOR HOUSE
stays.desc: If you're feeling fancy! This is the nicest of the three, right in town and great views of the harbor.

stays.name: ISLAND INN

stays.name: EARTHBOX INN

things.title: THINGS TO DO
things.intro: There is lots to do on the island if you can spare the time!

items.name: WESTCOTT BAY SHELLFISH CO.
items.desc: The best oysters. Pulled straight from the bay and shucked at picnic tables overlooking the water.

items.name: SAN JUAN ISLAND BREWING CO.
items.desc: A big, friendly taproom in the middle of town. Great for beer, cider, and some classic pub food.

items.name: SALTY FOX
items.desc: Our go-to coffee spot with breakfast snacks.

sections.title: ACTIVITIES
sections.photoAlt: A boat crossing the water off San Juan Island

items.name: WHALE WATCHING
items.desc: Could be whale-y fun! Lots of different types of whales hang out near the island, Orcas, humpbacks, etc.

items.name: VISIT ALPACAS
items.desc: Go hang out with some alpacas. Pet them?

sections.title: SIGHTS
sections.photoAlt: A marina in the San Juan Islands

items.name: LIME KILN POINT STATE PARK
items.desc: A lighthouse on the west-side rocks and your best shot at spotting orcas from shore.

items.name: ROCHE HARBOR
items.desc: A historic resort village on the north end of the island. East-coast vibes.

items.name: PELINDABA LAVENDER FARM
items.desc: Fields of lavender in bloom in July! Plus a farm stand of everything-lavender.

items.name: NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK
items.desc: American Camp and English Camp. Beach walks, prairie trails, and big views at both ends of the island.

items.a: Yep, if you're staying at one of our recommended hotels. All three are under a 0.5 mile walk and relatively flat.

For the weekend overall, we're aiming for "Western Elegance," with a more casual Friday welcome event (i.e., bolo ties, cowboy boots, cowboy hats welcome). Inspo here.
